Replaced by Arca 0.6.0 (v0.6.0, d0ce9dae), a breaking minor release (DF-ARCA-2026-0014: only a provider confirms a write). EntryState, QueueEntry, OfflineQueue and CommitReceipt are opaque: they read with the same patterns but cannot be constructed or copy-and-updated outside Arca; a CommitReceipt carries the idempotency key of the operation it confirms, and OfflineQueue.recordResult and recordReconciliation refuse another operation's receipt with the new QueueError.ReceiptMismatch. The persisted queue format (arcaQueue 1) is unchanged. The packages' license changes from MIT (0.5.0) to PolyForm-Noncommercial-1.0.0 (0.6.0); the owner (kemiller2002) explicitly accepted that change. Conditor has no Arca descriptor: it installs the set's selection from its release-asset NuGet feed against the Registry's sha256 (released Conditor 0.10.17, REG-RU-007, conditor#120). Known consumer incompatibility, not a VER-003 exception: Chrona declares arca 0.5.0 in its conditor.json and its store code (for example src/Chrona.Application/Store/StoreSync.fs and src/Chrona.Domain/Persistence.fs) uses EntryState, QueueEntry, OfflineQueue and CommitReceipt in ways 0.6.0 refuses, so it does not compile against 0.6.0. The owner decided on 2026-10-28 that 1.32.0 ships Arca 0.6.0 and Chrona stays on 1.31.0 until it migrates; Conditor 0.10.17's CI proves Chrona's 1.32.0 plan names Arca 0.5.0 -> 0.6.0 and Forma 0.10.0 -> 0.11.0 and does not apply it (conditor 6df8c4c). The set itself is consistent: EchelonFoundry.Fides.Arca 0.2.0 needs Arca.Core >= 0.1.0, EchelonFoundry.Arca.Limen 0.6.0 needs limen-fsharp >= 0.9.0 (selected 0.9.0), and no component failed qualification
